meanings.usage: 常用于口语中表示打扰某人

meanings.meaning: 烦恼（常用a spot of bother表示小麻烦） verb. 打扰

meanings.usage: 英式英语中常用，美式英语用apartment
正式用词，指严厉地批评或责备
指由于不注意而造成的错误或疏忽
形容做事深思熟虑、小心谨慎
指在困难情况下保持冷静的能力
指隐藏在暗处等待时机
指手指留下的纹路，用于身份识别
指某事令人难以想象或相信
原指喜鹊，因其收集习惯比喻爱收集东西的人
指储藏钱或物品以备将来使用
指为寻找东西而翻遍某处
珠宝的总称，不可数名词
指打断某人的活动或使某人担忧
形容人对小事过分担心或挑剔

phrases.usage: 表示小麻烦、小纠纷，是英语中常用的委婉表达

examples.en: She described it as a little spot of bother.
examples.zh: 她把这描述为一点小麻烦。

phrases.usage: 指通过武力或强行手段进入某处

examples.en: Burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
examples.zh: 窃贼趁她不在时强行闯入了。

phrases.usage: 表示在某人这个年纪，常用于表达某种行为是否适合某人的年龄

examples.en: At her age, it might be more prudent to have someone with her.
examples.zh: 在她这个年纪，有人陪着可能更明智。

phrases.usage: 指把东西翻过来或翻遍

examples.en: Everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over.
examples.zh: 她的所有东西都被扔了出来，翻了个遍。

examples.en: She regained her composure and was ready to search.
examples.zh: 她恢复了镇定，准备开始搜查。

phrases.usage: 表示不是第一次做某事，暗示之前有过类似经历

examples.en: Their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day.
examples.zh: 他们进入这间公寓显然不是当天第一次作案。

phrases.usage: 指打电话，是口语中常见的表达

examples.en: She rang up her daughter and asked for help.
examples.zh: 她给女儿打电话请求帮助。

examples.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats.
examples.zh: 老太太很高兴回到她住的公寓。

examples.en: Her basket had grown heavier with every step.
examples.zh: 她的篮子每走一步就重一些。

phrases.usage: 比喻某事非常清楚、显而易见

examples.en: It was as clear as daylight that burglars had forced an entry.
examples.zh: 显而易见，窃贼强行闯入了。

grammar.title: 过去完成时 (Past Perfect Tense)
grammar.definition: 表示在过去某一时刻之前已经完成的动作，常用于描述过去的背景或先发生的事件 当需要表达'过去的过去'这一概念时使用，常与when, after, before等连用，或用于宾语从句中

examples.en: She had gone shopping after the home help had left.
examples.zh: 她在管家离开后才去购物。

examples.en: She had shut them before going out.
examples.zh: 她在出门前把门都关上了。

examples.en: The burglars must have been disturbed.

grammar.title: 过去进行时 (Past Continuous Tense)
grammar.definition: 表示在过去某一时刻正在进行的动作，或用来描述过去的背景 常用于描述故事发生的背景，或与when/while等连用表示两个同时进行的动作

examples.en: Her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest.
examples.zh: 她满脑子想的都是午餐和好好休息。

examples.en: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help.
examples.zh: 她正想着第二天早上一定要责备她的管家。

grammar.title: must have + 过去分词
grammar.definition: 表示对过去发生的事情的推测，意为'一定/肯定做过某事' 用于根据现有证据或情况对过去事件进行肯定性的推测

examples.en: She must reprimand her home help.

patterns.pattern: 主语 + be glad to + 动词原形

original.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats.
original.zh: 老太太很高兴回到她住的公寓。

imitations.en: I was glad to see my old friends again.
imitations.zh: 我很高兴再次见到我的老朋友们。

imitations.en: She was glad to finish her work on time.
imitations.zh: 她很高兴按时完成了工作。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + be/feel + 形容词 + to + 动词原形

original.en: At her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her.
original.zh: 在她这个年纪，有人陪着可能更明智。

imitations.en: It might be better to wait for the police.
It is wise to check everything carefully.
imitations.zh: 仔细检查一切是明智的。

original.en: It was as clear as daylight that burglars had forced an entry.
original.zh: 显而易见，窃贼强行闯入了。

imitations.en: It is obvious that she has been robbed.
It is certain that he will come tomorrow.

patterns.pattern: 主语 + had + 过去分词 + before + doing something

original.en: She had shut them before going out.
original.zh: 她在出门前把门都关上了。

imitations.en: He had finished his homework before watching TV.
imitations.zh: 他在看电视前已经完成了作业。

imitations.en: I had locked the door before leaving.
imitations.zh: 我离开前已经锁好了门。

lines.en: The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats where she lived.
lines.zh: 老妇人回到了她居住的公寓楼，心里很高兴。

lines.en: Her shopping had tired her and her basket ad grown heavier with every step of the way home.
lines.zh: 去商店买东西把她搞得筋疲力尽；在回家的路上，她每走一步，就感到手里的篮子又重了一点。

lines.en: In the life her thoughts were on lunch and a good rest; but when she got out at her own floor, both were forgotten in her sudden discovery that her front door was open.
lines.zh: 她乘上电梯后，只想着午餐和好好休息一下。但她到自己的楼层走出电梯后，就把这两件事忘了个干净，因为她突然发现她家的大门开着。

lines.en: She was thinking that she must reprimand her home help the next morning for such a monstrous piece of negligence , when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left and she knew that she had turned both keys in their locks, She walked slowly into the hall and at once noticed that all the room doors were open, yet following her regular practice she had shut them before going out.
lines.zh: 她心想明天上午一定要好好训斥那个干家务的帮手，她竟如此疏忽大意。但突然记起来了，帮手是在她出去买东西之前走的，她还记得曾用了两把钥匙把大门锁上了。她慢慢地走进前厅，立即发现所有的房门都敞开着，而她记得在出门买东西前，她按老规矩是把房门一一锁上的。

lines.en: Looking into the drawing room, she saw a scene of confusion over by her writing desk.
lines.zh: 她往起居室里看去，写字台边一片狼籍。

lines.en: It was as clear as daylight then that burglars had forced an entry during her absence.
lines.zh: 事情很清楚，在她外出时，窃贼曾闯进家门。

lines.en: Her first impulse was to go round all the rooms looking for the thieves, but then she decided that at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her, so she went to fetch the porter from his basement.
lines.zh: 她第一个条件反射是各个房间搜寻一下窃贼，但转念一想，像她这个年纪，最好找个人一起去。于是她到地下室去找看门的人。

lines.en: By this time her legs were beginning to tremble, so she sat down and accepted a cup of very strong tea, while he telephoned the police.
lines.zh: 这时她两腿累得开始发抖，于是坐了下来，喝了一杯浓茶。与此同时，看门的人给警察挂了电话。

lines.en: Then, her composure regained , she was ready to set off with the porter's assistance to search for nay intruders who might still be lurking in her flat.
lines.zh: 此刻老妇人也镇定了下来，准备在看门人的协助下搜寻可能仍躲藏在她房里的窍贼。

lines.en: They went through the rooms, being careful to touch nothing, as they did not want to hinder the police in their search for fingerprints .
lines.zh: 他俩搜遍这每一个房间，小心翼翼地不接触任何东西，因为他们怕妨碍警察寻找指纹。
房间里的紊乱状况是无法想像的。

lines.en: She had lived in the flat for thirty years and was a veritable magpie at hoarding ; and it seemed as though everything she possessed had been tossed out and turned over and over.
lines.zh: 老妇人在这套公寓里住了30年，她又是个名副其实的收藏家。看来她的每一件东西都被翻了出来，并且被里里外外看了遍。

lines.en: At least sorting out the things she should have discarded years ago was now being made easier for her.
lines.zh: 这样一来，她倒是容易将那些几年前就该扔掉的东西找出来了。

lines.en: Then a police inspector arrived with a constable and she told them of her discovery of the ransacked flat.
lines.zh: 过了一会儿，一位巡官带着一名警察来了。

lines.en: The inspector began to look for fingerprints, while the constable checked that the front door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
lines.zh: 她向他们讲述了发现公寓遭劫的经过。巡官开始搜寻指纹，警察经检查发现大门锁头并无撬过的迹象。

lines.en: There was no trace of fingerprints, but the inspector found a dirty red bundle that contained jewellery which the old lady said was not hers.
lines.zh: 由此可以证明，窍贼或者是用万能钥匙，或者是翻越阳台进来的。巡官没有发现指纹，却发现了一个装有珠宝的、肮脏的红包袱。

lines.en: So their entry into this flat was apparently not the burglars' first job that day and they must have been disturbed.
lines.zh: 老妇人说那不是她的。很明显，闯进这套公寓的窃贼那天并不是首次作案，而且他一定受了惊吓。

lines.en: The inspector then asked the old lady to try to check what was missing by the next day and advised her not to stay alone in the flat for a few nights.
lines.zh: 巡官请老妇人在次日之前设法查清丢了些什么，并劝她几夜之内不要独自一人在公寓过夜。

lines.en: The old lady though the was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him, she rang up her daughter and asked for her help in what she described as a little spot of bother.
lines.zh: 老妇人觉得巡官大惊小怪，但既然看门人也同意他的意见，她只得打电话向女儿求援，说她碰到了一点儿小麻烦。

questions.q: What did the old lady find when she got home?
questions.zh: 老妇人到家时发现了什么？
questions.a: She found her front door open, all the room doors open, and the drawing room in confusion over by her writing desk, which showed that burglars had forced an entry.
questions.aZh: 她发现自家大门开着，所有房门也都敞着，起居室写字台边一片狼藉，说明窃贼曾闯入。
questions.hint: 答案出自课文开头到'as clear as daylight'一段：出电梯发现大门开着，进厅见房门全开。

questions.q: Why did the old lady no longer blame her home help?
questions.zh: 老妇人为什么不再责怪她的家务帮手？
questions.a: Because she remembered she had gone shopping after the home help had left, and she knew she had turned both keys in their locks herself.
questions.aZh: 因为她想起帮手是在她外出购物之前就离开了，而且她记得自己曾用两把钥匙把大门锁上。
questions.hint: 见'must reprimand her home help…when she remembered that she had gone shopping after the home help had left'一句。

questions.q: Why did she go to fetch the porter instead of searching the rooms alone?
questions.zh: 她为何不独自搜查房间，而是去找看门人？
questions.a: Because at her age she thought it might be more prudent to have someone with her.
questions.aZh: 因为她觉得像自己这个年纪，最好有人陪着一起，更为稳妥。
questions.hint: 见'at her age it might be more prudent to have someone with her'一句。

questions.q: What did the constable's check of the front door prove?
questions.zh: 警察检查大门后证明了什么？
questions.a: It proved the locks had not been forced, so the burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
questions.aZh: 这证明门锁没有被撬过，因此窃贼或是用了万能钥匙，或是翻越阳台进来的。
questions.hint: 见'checked that the front door locks had not been forced, thereby proving that…either…or…'。

questions.q: The inspector advised her not to stay alone. Did the old lady agree with him, and how do we know?
questions.zh: 巡官劝她不要独自过夜，老妇人同意他的意见吗？文中哪句可以看出？
questions.a: She did not really agree — she thought he was a fussy creature. But since the porter agreed with him, she still rang up her daughter for help.
questions.aZh: 她其实并不认同——她觉得巡官是个大惊小怪的人；但因为看门人也赞同他，她最终还是打电话向女儿求助。
questions.hint: 见结尾'The old lady thought he was a fussy creature, but since the porter agreed with him…'。

translation:
老妇人回到了她居住的公寓楼，心里很高兴。
去商店买东西把她搞得筋疲力尽；在回家的路上，她每走一步，就感到手里的篮子又重了一点。
她乘上电梯后，只想着午餐和好好休息一下。
但她到自己的楼层走出电梯后，就把这两件事忘了个干净，因为她突然发现她家的大门开着。
她心想明天上午一定要好好训斥那个干家务的帮手，她竟如此疏忽大意。
但突然记起来了，帮手是在她出去买东西之前走的，她还记得曾用了两把钥匙把大门锁上了。
她慢慢地走进前厅，立即发现所有的房门都敞开着，而她记得在出门买东西前，她按老规矩是把房门一一锁上的。
她往起居室里看去，写字台边一片狼籍。
事情很清楚，在她外出时，窃贼曾闯进家门。
她第一个条件反射是各个房间搜寻一下窃贼，但转念一想，像她这个年纪，最好找个人一起去。
于是她到地下室去找看门的人。
这时她两腿累得开始发抖，于是坐了下来，喝了一杯浓茶。
与此同时，看门的人给警察挂了电话。
此刻老妇人也镇定了下来，准备在看门人的协助下搜寻可能仍躲藏在她房里的窍贼。
他俩搜遍这每一个房间，小心翼翼地不接触任何东西，因为他们怕妨碍警察寻找指纹。
房间里的紊乱状况是无法想像的。
老妇人在这套公寓里住了30年，她又是个名副其实的收藏家。
看来她的每一件东西都被翻了出来，并且被里里外外看了遍。
这样一来，她倒是容易将那些几年前就该扔掉的东西找出来了。
过了一会儿，一位巡官带着一名警察来了。
她向他们讲述了发现公寓遭劫的经过。
巡官开始搜寻指纹，警察经检查发现大门锁头并无撬过的迹象。
由此可以证明，窍贼或者是用万能钥匙，或者是翻越阳台进来的。
巡官没有发现指纹，却发现了一个装有珠宝的、肮脏的红包袱。
老妇人说那不是她的。
很明显，闯进这套公寓的窃贼那天并不是首次作案，而且他一定受了惊吓。
巡官请老妇人在次日之前设法查清丢了些什么，并劝她几夜之内不要独自一人在公寓过夜。
老妇人觉得巡官大惊小怪，但既然看门人也同意他的意见，她只得打电话向女儿求援，说她碰到了一点儿小麻烦。
title: A Spot of Bother
subtitle: 一点小麻烦

lead.question: 购物回家的老妇人发现家中疑遭盗窃，这'一点小麻烦'究竟怎么回事？
lead.warmup: 一位独居的老妇人购物回家，拖着越来越沉的篮子回到住了三十年的公寓，只想吃顿午餐、好好休息。可她走出电梯却发现自家大门敞开，屋里所有房门也都打开，写字台边一片狼藉。是虚惊一场，还是真的遭了贼？学完本课，你不仅能读懂这段幽默的推理故事，还能学会用英语轻描淡写地说出'小麻烦'。
goals: 掌握 bother、spot、nuisance 等描述'小麻烦'的名词及搭配
学会用 must have done、should have done 表达对过去的推测与虚拟
理解 with 短语、现在分词短语作状语，以及 it 作形式主语的用法
能用 where / that / which 引导的定语从句描写地点与物品
lead.summary: 购物回家的老妇人在公寓门口发现大门敞开、房门尽开，写字台边一片狼藉，断定窃贼在她外出时闯入。她请来看门人并报警。警察发现门锁未被撬，推测窃贼或用万能钥匙、或翻越阳台；现场没有指纹，只留下一个装着别人珠宝的红包袱，可见窃贼受了惊。最后她嫌巡官大惊小怪，却仍向女儿求援，自嘲不过是'一点小麻烦'。
lead.tips: 'a spot of bother' 是英式口语里故作轻松的说法，只表示'一点小麻烦'，别误译成'一块污点'；bother 此处是名词，语气比 trouble 轻得多。

exercises.q: 汉译英：我碰到了一点儿小麻烦，你能帮我一把吗？
exercises.a: I've run into a spot of bother — could you give me a hand?
exercises.note: spot of bother 是轻描淡写的'小麻烦'

exercises.q: 汉译英：窃贼一定受了惊吓，所以那天没能得手。
exercises.a: The burglars must have been disturbed, so they failed to finish the job that day.
exercises.note: must have done 表对过去的肯定推测

exercises.q: 句型转换：用 it 作形式主语改写 'To have someone with her might be more prudent.'
exercises.a: It might be more prudent to have someone with her.
exercises.note: it 作形式主语，真正主语后置

exercises.q: 填空：At least sorting out the things she ____ ____ discarded years ago was now made easier for her.
exercises.note: should have done 表本该做却未做

exercises.q: 填空：Her basket had grown heavier ____ every step of the way home.
exercises.note: with 短语作伴随状语，表逐渐变化

exercises.q: 改错：The old lady was glad to be back at the block of flats which she lived.
exercises.note: 先行词表地点，用关系副词 where

exercises.q: 汉译英：楼上传来的噪音真是个麻烦，吵得我一夜没睡好。
exercises.a: The noise from upstairs was a real nuisance — it kept me awake all night.
exercises.note: nuisance 指令人讨厌的人或事

quiz.q: 老妇人回到家，首先在自家门口发现了什么异常？
options: Her front door was open.
Her basket had been stolen.
The porter was waiting for her by the lift.
Her daughter had already arrived.
quiz.note: 课文开头：her front door was open

quiz.q: 标题里的 'a spot of bother' 最贴切的意思是？
options: a small mark on the wall
a little trouble
a short rest
a spot of tea
quiz.note: spot of bother 意为'一点小麻烦'

quiz.q: 老妇人为什么没有责怪她的家务帮手？
options: Because the home help had locked all the doors.
Because she had gone shopping after the home help left and had locked both keys herself.
Because the home help had that day off.
Because the porter told her not to blame her.
quiz.note: 她想起帮手走后自己才出门并上了锁

quiz.q: 警察检查门锁后，得出的结论是什么？
options: The front door had been forced open.
The old lady had simply forgotten to lock the door.
The burglars had either used skeleton keys or entered over the balcony.
The home help had left the door open.
quiz.note: locks 未被撬 → 万能钥匙或翻阳台

quiz.q: 现场那个肮脏的红包袱说明了什么？
options: It belonged to the old lady.
The inspector had left it there by mistake.
The burglars were not working there for the first time that day and had been disturbed.
The porter had hidden it under the desk.
quiz.note: not the burglars' first job…must have been disturbed

quiz.q: 故事结尾，老妇人为什么还是打电话向女儿求助？
options: Because the porter agreed with the inspector, so she gave in and asked for help.
Because her daughter had telephoned her first.
Because the police ordered her to leave the flat.
Because she wanted to hire a new home help.
quiz.note: since the porter agreed with him…she rang up her daughter
